roles.title: Vice-President
roles.description:
CodeStarters is a student-led nonprofit in Cupertino that teaches CS and AI to younger students and builds free websites for local businesses. Programs include: CS & AI Education (intro AI, AI literacy & safety, web basics), AI Development & Agent Engineering (OpenClaw + Hermes, agent workflows + OpenCode), summer bootcamps, Fire Hacks hackathon, and free websites for Cupertino businesses.

ROLE: Vice-President (Leadership)

EXPECTATIONS: Strong organizational skills, reliable follow-through, comfortable representing CodeStarters to partners and the community, able to coordinate across CS, AI, marketing, and events teams.

- Posted a meme response or sarcastic reply to the accusation.
- Ignored the business owner's concerns or let marketing handle it without oversight.

- Make no operational changes, only focus on PR.

- Leave her alone with the sponsor VP.
- Ignore the incident to protect the $5k.

- Decide on a hard cap with the President and Head of AI — do not allow unlimited growth.

- Provide immediate relief for mentors: reduce their load, hire alumni, merge sections, or offer stipends — choose at least one.
- Address the two quitting mentors: have a retention conversation this week with a concrete plan for reducing their load.
STRONG:
- Offer 45 confirmed spots plus a structured waitlist of 97 with rolling admission dates.
- Set a target for mentor hours capped per week (e.g., max 10) and explain how to achieve this.
- Suggest a growth headline alternative for the President that doesn't promise unlimited seats.
RED FLAGS:
- Accept all 142 with the same number of mentors.
- Ignore the waitlisted families.
- Let the two mentors quit without a plan to redistribute their responsibilities.
- Focus on growth for PR without discussing quality or burnout.

- Hold the volunteer accountable: revoke their access, document the conversation, and change their role if needed.
